text:
kevin: Quick heads-up — a customer hit a nasty flow where repeated 429s + context truncation during our embeddings migration made the UI show gibberish. Our error-ref page mentions fallback behavior but has no concrete SDK example. Can someone pair on a tiny snippet + a one-paragraph runbook we can drop into the guide?

sarah: I can take the snippet. Do we want JS and Python? Might be overkill; a single pattern with pseudocode could be fine.

maya: +1 on both languages. The most common ask is: detect 429, trim context, downgrade model/shorten max_tokens, and retry with exponential backoff. Keep it 6–10 lines.

jordan: Also include telemetry hints: tag the retry type (context_trim vs model_fallback) so the console can surface when users are hitting this. We have a tracing field `retry_reason` in the SDK already.

sarah: OK, rough draft for Python (will add comments):
```python
# minimal pattern: detect 429, trim context, fallback to smaller model, retry once
try:
    res = client.generate(model="redwood-large-v1", prompt=long_prompt, max_tokens=1024)
except RateLimitError as e:
    # record why we retried
    client.metrics.increment("retry", tags={"retry_reason": "context_trim"})
    shorter = trim_context(long_prompt, keep_last_tokens=2048)
    res = client.generate(model="redwood-small-v1", prompt=shorter, max_tokens=256)
```

kevin: This is great. Can you add a one-paragraph "why" blurb explaining tradeoffs (quality vs latency/cost)? Also mention when to avoid automatic downgrades (sensitive generation that must use large model).

sarah: Added the blurb in my head :) Will open PR after I format the JS snippet.

maya: For the runbook: short checklist bullets we can paste into the error-ref: 1) reproduce with minimal prompt, 2) confirm 429s are rate-limit and not infra, 3) try trimmed context locally, 4) add fallback snippet, 5) monitor fallback rate in Console. Keep it 5 bullets.

jordan: One more: link to existing SDK `retry_reason` docs and to the Console tag dashboard. I can add the dashboard link once PR is up.

sarah: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/612 — includes Python + JS examples, runbook bullets, and a short note about telemetry. PTAL @kevin @jordan.

kevin: Reviewing now. My only ask: make the JS snippet show both a backoff and an immediate model fallback (so frontends have an option to surface a "degraded experience" banner).

sarah: Will update.

docs-bot: Automated check: lint OK, broken links scanner found one relative link in the runbook that points to /old-errref — suggest replacement /error-reference/429.

sarah: Thanks @docs-bot — fixing link in the PR now.

maya: Once merged, can we also add a short example in the migration guide that demonstrates instrumentation (console event name + tag) so customers can map their incidents to our guidance?

jordan: Yes, add a single sentence with the event name `client.retry` + tags `retry_reason` and `fallback_model`. That should be enough.

kevin: LGTM, approving once the JS backoff example is added. Thanks all — landing this will unblock a support thread. :thumbsup:

sarah: Done — pushed the JS patch and updated the runbook link. PR ready for final merge.

kevin: Merged. Can someone add a short note to release notes (docs changelog) so support teams can cite it?

maya: I'll add a one-liner to the changelog: "Added 429+context-trim runbook & SDK fallback snippets (Python/JS) — guidance for graceful degrade flows."

kevin: Perfect. Closing the loop here. If support sees another repro, we'll iterate on the sample.
